## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a Path tab (native path trace, Linux only; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row prefills it)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

go run .

mise run run          # Build and run

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

1	# Container engine, OCI registries, network diagnostics, sockets and interfaces
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## The container engine — `internal/engine` and `internal/docker`
7	
8	**`internal/engine`** names the engine in use — docker or podman — and carries
9	everything that is not the same between the two: the binary, the credential
10	helper prefix, the auth file, the host socket, and the `--format` templates. It
11	is its own package rather than a field of `internal/docker` because
12	`internal/scan` needs the same answer and does not import `internal/docker` —
13	`internal/forge`'s arrangement read one level down (§3.67).
14	
15	`engine.Resolve(preference)` turns `app.container_engine` into a `Shape`:
16	`auto` takes docker if it is on PATH and podman otherwise; a pinned engine that
17	is absent is an **error**, never the other one, because the two do not hold the
18	same containers. Anything else is taken as a path to a binary. The router
19	resolves once at startup and once per context switch, into `engine.SetCurrent`.
20	
21	A `Shape` carries **no resolved filesystem path**: `AuthPaths()`, `AuthPath()`
22	and `HostSocket()` are methods. The shape is built at package initialisation, so
23	a `$HOME` read there would be frozen before anything else runs — and whether the
24	socket exists is the whole question, since `podman system service` can start or
25	stop while the application is up.
26	
27	**`internal/docker`** drives that engine. Every invocation goes through one
28	seam — `dockerRunner`, implemented by `cliRunner` (`exec.go`) — which is what
29	made podman cheap: the binary name lived in exactly one place. The package is
30	split by resource: `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`, `volumes.go`,
31	`registry.go`, `system.go`, `launch.go`, plus `exec.go` (the seam), `parse.go`,
32	`container_ports.go`, `identifier.go` and `names.go`. It is **not** called
33	`internal/container`: renaming it would touch 40 files for a vocabulary gain.
34	
35	Two things about the engine are worth knowing before changing this code:
36	
37	- **The `--format` templates are per engine and identical today.** Podman
38	  implements `--format`, but equality of the *fields* is guaranteed nowhere, and
39	  a divergence raises no error — it produces wrong rows. No measurement has been
40	  taken against a real podman; `TestTheTwoTemplateSetsAreStillUnmeasured` fails
41	  the day the two sets stop matching, so a divergence is recorded deliberately.
42	- **`system df -v` is scraped, not templated**, and is therefore disabled under
43	  podman (`Shape.ParsesSystemDFVerbose`). It is a fixed-width table read at
44	  offsets taken from its header line, and there is no `--format` that exposes
45	  per-image unique size.
46	
47	- **Three typed, read-only reads for the Path tab** (`container_network.go`,
48	  DEVDESK-330), each with a `context.Context` that kills the invocation:
49	  `InspectContainerNetworking(ctx, id)`, `ListContainersContext(ctx, all)`
50	  (`ListContainers(all)` is unchanged and does not use it) and
51	  `EngineOperatingSystem(ctx)`. They run `container inspect`, `ps` and `info`
52	  and nothing else. `InspectContainerNetworking` runs
53	  `container inspect --format <containerNetworkingFormat> <id>`: the format
54	  selects `Name`, `HostConfig.NetworkMode`, `State.Running` and, per network,
55	  `IPAddress`, `Gateway` and `GwPriority`, so `Config.Env`, labels and mounts are
56	  never read into memory. It reads stdout only, and its error carries the
57	  command label, never the output. The ID must pass `IsContainerID` and is one
58	  argv element, never a name. The inspect and `info` reads refuse a non-Docker
59	  engine with `ErrDockerOnly` before any invocation; output over 256 KiB
60	  (`maxInspectBytes`) is refused. `InspectContainer`, which returns the whole
61	  `docker inspect` JSON (secrets included) with stdout and stderr merged and no
62	  context, was not reused for that reason. The `info` format
63	  (`{{.OperatingSystem}}`) is a docker-only literal and is not in
64	  `engine.Templates`.
65	- `internal/docker/netdiag.go` — **gone**. §3.33 took the five probes that did not need a container, §3.43 the ports table, §3.44 the topology (and with it `docker/topology.go` and the last `--privileged`), §3.47 the route trace and the file itself (the trace came back in the process as `internal/nettrace`, DEVDESK-327). §3.61 removed the OCI connectivity test, and with it the last container this application runs for a diagnostic: `networks.go` now holds only `ListNetworks`, `CreateNetwork`, `RemoveNetwork`, `PruneNetworks` and `InspectNetwork`.
66	
67	## OCI registries — `internal/oci`
68	
69	`internal/oci/oci.go` — an OCI **registry** HTTP client: list tags,
70	download and extract a tar.gz (a repository template is one — `templates.md`). It speaks the distribution spec over `net/http`
71	and never shells out, so it is engine-agnostic and podman changed nothing in it.
72	
73	**Typed status errors and context variants (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** A registry
74	or token endpoint answering with a non-success status returns
75	`*oci.StatusError{Code, Source, Challenge}`; read it with `errors.As`. `Source`
76	is `SourceRegistry` (the v2 API) or `SourceToken` (the Bearer token endpoint).
77	`Challenge` is the `Www-Authenticate` header of a 401 whose challenge is not
78	Bearer. `Error()` keeps the three historical messages to the character
79	(`registry returned 404`, `token endpoint returned 403`,
80	`unexpected auth challenge: ...`), so nothing on screen or in a log changed.
81	Failures that are not a status (unreadable body, missing realm, no token
82	field) stay plain errors and do not match `errors.As`.
83	
84	The unexported `unexpectedChallenge` field is a deviation from the plan, which
85	had only `Code`, `Source` and `Challenge`: with those three, a 401 with a
86	non-Bearer challenge and a 401 returned by the registry after a token exchange
87	both read `Source == SourceRegistry`, `Code == 401`, and `Error()` could not
88	give each its own message. The flag tells them apart without widening the
89	exported surface.
90	
91	`ListRegistryTagsContext` and the `...Context` variants of `registryGET`,
92	`registryDo`, `doRequest` and `exchangeBearerToken` take a `context.Context`
93	(the token endpoint request included) and check `ctx.Err()` at the head of
94	every page. The old names delegate with `context.Background()`, signatures
95	unchanged. A deadline or a cancel reaches the caller as an error that
96	satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` or `context.Canceled`,
97	and never as a `StatusError`. **Limit:** `registryHTTPClient` keeps its own
98	`Timeout: 15s` per request, and the client wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`
99	for that timeout too. A caller cannot tell the client timeout from the
100	context's deadline, so `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts both in
101	the `failed` verdict.
102	
103	**Credentials stay on their origin (DEVDESK-410).** Three guards keep the Basic
104	credentials and the Bearer token from leaving the registry they were meant for:
105	
106	- **The tag list never follows a `Link: rel="next"` to another origin.**
107	  `ListRegistryTagsContext` checks each `next` with `sameOrigin` (the catalog
108	  walker's guard) before the next request. A foreign `next` is an error that
109	  wraps `ErrTagsNextOffOrigin` (test it with `errors.Is`) and names the
110	  destination host only. No partial list is returned: a short list could pass
111	  for the whole one, and `imageupdate` and the security remediation would read
112	  a false "up to date". The catalog walker behaves otherwise: it returns
113	  `truncated=true` with the names already read, and no error.
114	- **`registryHTTPClient` has a `CheckRedirect`, `refuseOffOriginRedirect`.** A
115	  redirect is refused when its scheme, host or port differ from the first
116	  request of the chain (`via[0]`, not only the previous hop), so a chain that
117	  leaves the origin and comes back is refused too. The error reads
118	  `refusing redirect to another origin (<host>)` and wraps
119	  `errOffOriginRedirect` (`errors.Is`). It holds neither the target URL, nor
120	  its path or query: `redirectRefusal` strips the `*url.Error` that carries
121	  them, so a signed URL reaches neither the footer nor the logs. The limit of 10 redirects (`maxRedirects`, the `net/http` default) is
122	  kept. It applies to everything that uses the client: tags, catalog and the
123	  token endpoint.
124	- **The token endpoint's answer is capped at 1 MiB** (`maxTokenResponse`). A
125	  larger body is an error (`token response over 1048576 bytes`), not a silent
126	  cut.
127	
128	**Behavior change.** Some redirects that were followed are now refused: `http`
129	to `https` on the same host, `host` to `host:443`, and a host written with a
130	different case. The comparison is on the exact scheme and `host:port`, and the
131	guard refuses when in doubt.
132	
133	**Catalog walk (DEVDESK-306, IS-03).** `ListCatalogContext(ctx, apiURL,
134	username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` returns `(names, truncated, err)`. It
135	asks `<apiURL>/v2/_catalog?n=<pageSize>` and follows `Link: rel="next"` for at
136	most `maxPages` pages (non-positive limits are an error). `truncated` is true
137	when names were left: the page cap was reached with a `next` link, more than
138	`maxPages*pageSize` names came back (the list is cut to that), or the `next`
139	link points to another origin. Each page body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger
140	page is an error, not a silent cut. A non-200 answer is a `*StatusError`.
141	Authentication is the tags' flow: Basic, then Bearer on a challenge, the token
142	kept across pages.
143	
144	- **`next` is followed only to the same origin.** `sameOrigin` compares scheme
145	  and host strictly (`host` and `host:443` differ), so a registry cannot make
146	  the walk send the Basic credentials or the token elsewhere. A foreign or
147	  differently written `next` ends the walk as `truncated`, with no error.
148	- **HTTP 3xx redirects are hardened too** (DEVDESK-410): the walk goes through
149	  `registryHTTPClient`, whose `CheckRedirect` refuses a redirect to another
150	  origin (see "Credentials stay on their origin" above).

152	## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)
153	
154	Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
155	and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:
156	
157	- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
158	  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
159	  an anonymous entry, D12).
160	- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
161	- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
162	  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
163	  `library/` applied once (D39).
164	- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
165	  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
166	- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
167	  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
168	  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
169	  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
170	  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
171	  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
172	  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
173	  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
174	  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
175	  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
176	  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
177	  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
178	  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
179	- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
180	  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
181	  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
182	  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
183	  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
184	  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
185	  with no request at all. Production uses
186	  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
187	  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
188	  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
189	  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
190	- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
191	  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` and
192	  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
193	  registry. Steps, in order:
194	  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
195	     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
196	  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
197	     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
198	     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
199	     is returned as is, with no row.
200	  3. Guard R1 (before the filter): when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
201	     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
202	     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
203	     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
204	     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
205	     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
206	     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
207	     `partial` set, not an error.
208	  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
209	     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
210	  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
211	     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
212	     others are dropped.
213	  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
214	     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
215	     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.
216	
217	  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
218	  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
219	  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
220	  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
221	  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
222	  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search
223	  (DEVDESK-311, IS-07, `walks.go`): `WithSharedWalks(ctx)` puts a memo on the
224	  batch context and `CatalogSearcher` goes through `walkCatalog`, so a search
225	  queries `/v2/_catalog` once per API URL and identity. Without the memo
226	  (any other caller) every call walks on its own.
227	  - Key: the exact API URL (trailing slash ignored) and the identity, an
228	    HMAC-SHA256 of username and password under a random per-batch key: no
229	    secret is held in clear and the key prints no userinfo. Two identities
230	    never share a walk, because Harbor, Artifactory and GitLab filter the
231	    catalog per account. A `credentials` entry with no effective secret shares
232	    the walk of an anonymous entry. A member on another port or subdomain has
233	    another API URL and is not grouped.
234	  - Leader and followers: the first call for a key walks, the others wait (or
235	    return on their own context). It is a memo, not a singleflight: the key is
236	    kept after the walk, so a member arriving later reuses the result, and it
237	    dies with the batch (no cache between two searches).
238	  - A shared failure (a 503, say) is the same error for every member, so the
239	    same verdict (`failed` or `refused`), one message per entry. A result
240	    caused by the leader's own context ending is not memoized: followers
241	    already waiting on that flight receive the leader's context error (verdict
242	    `failed`), and only members arriving afterwards walk again. A
243	    panic in the leader gives followers a sentinel error (`errWalkAborted`),
244	    never an empty catalog.
245	  - `repo_prefix` filtering, `partial`, `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` and
246	    `Cached only` stay computed per member.
247	  - Unverified assumption: members of one host answer on the same
248	    `/v2/_catalog` (IS-16).
249	  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
250	  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
251	- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
252	  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
253	  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
254	  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
255	  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
256	  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
257	  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
258	  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
259	  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
260	  match wins:
261	  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
262	     given in both cases;
263	  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
264	  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
265	  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
266	     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
267	     token endpoint is a failure); any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is
268	     `failed`;
269	  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
270	     oversized body, invalid request.
271	
272	  `ErrQueryTooShort` and `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` are returned by
273	  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).

275	## Image updates — `internal/imageupdate` (§3.88)
276	
277	Three tables carry an **Update** column (`internal/ui/updatecol`): oci's Images
278	tab, the containers list, and the Remediation tab of a scan result. It shows an
279	arrow when the image's registry holds something newer, and says what:
280	
281	| Kind | When | Cell |
282	|---|---|---|
283	| `NewPatch` | the tag has ≥ 3 version components and a tag differing only by the last, same variant, is higher (`20.11.1-alpine` → `20.11.4-alpine`) | the arrow and the tag |
284	| `NewBuild` | the digest the tag points to now is none of the local image's digests | the arrow alone (`IconArrowDown`) |
285	
286	A newer patch wins over a new build. Every other state says why there is no
287	arrow, in grey — a blank used to stand for all of them, which in the
288	Remediation tab (bases rarely pinned, often not held locally) meant a column
289	that was silent without saying why:
290	
291	| Kind | Cell | When |
292	|---|---|---|
293	| `UpToDate` | the check mark | the local digest is the tag's |
294	| `Pending` | `IconHourglass` | no answer yet |
295	| `Failed` | `IconHelpCircle` | the registry did not answer (logged) |
296	| `LocalBuild` | `IconHammer` | images, containers: no registry digest |
297	| `NotLocal` | `IconCloud` | Remediation: unpinned, and not held by the engine |
298	| `Pinned` | `IconPin` | a digest with no tag: nothing can move |
299	| `None` | blank | the question does not apply (untagged image, unresolved `FROM`) |
300	
301	Every state but a newer patch is one glyph (`updatecol.Cell`): the words cost
302	eleven cells in the widest table there is, and the reason is still spelled out
303	by `G`'s greyed shortcut in the footer and by `?`. `Status.Label` keeps the
304	word, which is what the filter matches. `Evaluate` takes what "no local digest"
305	means to its caller (`LocalBuild` or `NotLocal`). The column's filter only matches an update's label, or `/ca`
306	would find every `local build`. A tag with fewer components (`3.20`,
307	`20`) has no patches of its own — it floats over them, so a new patch moves the
308	tag and the digest says it. That is also the only answer a floating tag
309	(§3.79) ever gets.
310	
311	**The registry's side is cached, the comparison is not.** `imageupdate.Check`
312	keeps, per reference, the tag's digest and the newer patch tag in
313	`~/.devdesk/cache/image-updates.json` — 6 hours for an answer, 30 minutes for a
314	failure (unknown repository, no credentials) so it is not asked on every
315	refresh. `Evaluate` compares with the local digests each time a row is built,
316	so a pull clears the arrow without asking the registry again.
317	
318	**Two requests at most per reference.** The digest is a `HEAD` on the manifest
319	(`oci.ManifestDigest`) accepting an OCI index and a Docker manifest list — a
320	multi-platform tag's digest is the index's, the one `docker pull` records in
321	`RepoDigests`. Docker Hub does not count a `HEAD` against its pull rate limit.
322	The tag list (`oci.ListRegistryTags`) is only read for a tag with a patch
323	component. At most four references are asked at once; credentials are the
324	engine's (`docker.GetStoredCreds`), as for the Remediation tab.
325	
326	**What each view compares with:**
327	
328	- *Images* — the image's own `RepoDigests`, now read by the same `image
329	  inspect` that reads its size (`templates().ImageInspect`). Only a tagged image
330	  **with** a digest is asked about: one built or loaded here has none, and its
331	  name would send the question to a registry that never heard of it.
332	- *Containers* — the digests of the image the container was **created from**
333	  (`docker.ContainerImageDigests`: `container inspect` for the image ID, then
334	  `image inspect`). After a pull the container still runs the old image, so the
335	  arrow stays until it is recreated — which is what it is there to say. The
336	  digests are read again only when the set of containers changes, not on every
337	  two-second refresh.
338	- *Remediation* — the digest the Dockerfile pins, or else the image the engine
339	  holds under that name (`docker.ImageRepoDigests`). A base the engine does not
340	  hold only gets the patch side.
341	
342	`imageupdate.Tracker` is what each view keeps between checks: the facts it has
343	and the references a check is out for, so a reload asks only what is new or
344	stale. Every view reaches the network through a package variable its tests
345	replace.
346	
347	**Updating — `G` on the Images tab.** It pulls what the column points at (the
348	newer patch tag, or the same tag again for a new build) and removes the image
349	it replaces, by ID and never forced. It refuses while any container, running
350	or stopped, was created from that image (`docker.ContainersUsingImage`, `ps -a
351	--filter ancestor=`): removing it would break the container, and keeping it
352	would leave the update half done. The check is made twice — from the engine's
353	container count to grey `G` (Rule 130; docker only, podman reports none), and
354	against the engine just before the pull, since a container can appear in
355	between. A pull that brings the image already held removes nothing
356	(`docker.SameImageID`). It runs as a pull job, so the row spins and `K` stops
357	it; every refusal and failure is a footer line naming why (the containers in
358	use, a failed pull, an old image that could not be removed).
359	
360	**On a narrow terminal**, the containers table drops the two gauges before
361	Update (they are `DropFirst`, §3.71), then the I/O counters, then Update. Both
362	gauges now need 180 columns instead of 160.
363	
364	**Not done**: a digest for a tag the engine holds under another name, and the
365	`podman` side of `RepoDigests` has not been measured against a real `podman
366	system service` — the field exists there under the same name.
367	
368	**From a container to its image — `J`** (§3.89). The containers view sends
369	`ociresources.FocusImageRequestMsg` with the image reference exactly as the
370	engine printed it; the router switches to the OCI view and hands it the
371	request, which waits for the first listing if the view was just built
372	(`deferUntilListed`, the same queue agents use). Matching is the OCI view's
373	(`imageMatches`, `focus.go`): an implicit `latest`, docker's `nginx` against
374	podman's `docker.io/library/nginx`, a registry port that is not a tag, a
375	`repo@sha256:` digest against `RepoDigests`, and a bare ID — what `ps` shows
376	once the tag has moved to a newer image. A search hiding the target is
377	dropped; an image that is no longer listed is a footer `Warn`. There is no
378	`esc` back: `:ct` returns, as from any other view.
379	
380	## The OCI tables and the activity column — `internal/ui/oci_resources` (DEVDESK-146, A-09a; DEVDESK-153, A-09b)
381	
382	The four tables of `:oci` (Images, Networks, Volumes, Registries) and the
383	registry browser's tag table are on the activity column (Rule 125; the router
384	side is in `app-shell.md`).
385	
386	**Periodic refresh and terminal focus (DEVDESK-210).** `refreshInterval` is 10 s
387	(a var, so a test can shorten it). `RefreshTickMsg` used to refresh once and
388	never again; it now re-arms `tickCmd()` on every tick. While `Model.blurred` is
389	set (from `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`) the tick only re-arms and skips
390	`refreshReads()` (images, scan cache, networks, volumes; it never scans, Rule
391	126). On the focus edge (`Resume`) it runs `refreshReads()` once, with no new tick.
392	
393	**Registry browser (DEVDESK-218, A-09a2).** The tag table
394	(`registry_browser.go`, built by `newTagTable`, which `ActivityTables` also uses
395	so the guard sees the real table open or not, as `oci/registry-browser`) takes
396	`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0, an 8th column; Registry, Tag and
397	Updated are 1 to 3 (`tagColumnTag` = 2, `tagColumnUpdated` = 3). `tagRow` holds
398	`Activity components.RowActivity` and `ScanRunning`, stamped by
399	`rebuildTagTable` from `components.DescribeRow` (scan and pull, `ociKinds`,
400	target `jobs.TargetKey(imageName)`) over the snapshot the router pushes through
401	`SetJobs(runs, failures, context)`; the cell at rest is empty. While a scan
402	really runs (not queued) the C/H/M/L cells hold `…` in `DimStyle`; a queued scan
403	or a pull keeps the counts. The blink phase arrives with `SetBlinkPhase` and
404	`WantsBlink` is true for a visible running tag row. Rule 116: Updated drops
405	under 102 columns, L under 84, M under 78, H under 72, C under 66; at 60 only
406	the dot, Registry and Tag remain. The browser has no spinner of its own
407	(DEVDESK-374): a search shows the shared activity dot in the footer
408	(`Searching registries...`), and `WantsBlink` is true while it runs. After the search the
409	footer describes the selected tag (`Status{Detail}`). `tagScanSpinnerIdx` and
410	the local frame are deleted. `DescribeRow` filters by context: a scan of another
411	context no longer shows on a tag (D108).
412	
413	**Cancelling a lot and ignoring late answers (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** The
414	browser launches requests in lots (one per validation that starts something).
415	`browserGen` is a package-wide `atomic.Uint64`, incremented only from `Update`
416	(`nextBrowserGen`). `beginRequests()` cancels the previous lot (one
417	`CancelFunc`, `cancelRequests`, per lot, not per registry), takes a new
418	generation and resets `pendingSearches`; the `context` is born in `Update`
419	(Rule 110). `MultiRegistryTagsLoadedMsg`, `MultiRegistryTagsMetaMsg` and
420	`ImageSearchResultMsg` carry the `Gen` they were started with, and their
421	handlers return before logging anything when it differs from the open
422	browser's. The counter is global rather than per browser so that a browser
423	closed and reopened, or a new `Model` after a context switch, cannot accept the
424	answer of an older instance. `closeMultiRegistryBrowser` calls
425	`cancelInFlight()`, which also covers closing through `G` (a pull). A validation
426	that starts nothing (empty name, no registry checked) cancels nothing and
427	leaves `gen` alone. The tag lookups go through the `listRegistryTags` variable
428	(`oci.ListRegistryTagsContext`), the seam tests swap to capture the context;
429	there is no deadline on a tag lookup, only `maxTagPages` and the per-request
430	client timeout. `Model.RegistryBrowserGen()` exposes the generation to tests
431	only.
432	
433	**Level 1: image search (DEVDESK-299, IS-01; Open Tags DEVDESK-300, IS-11).**
434	The browser has three states: `browserStateInput` (form), `browserStateImages`
435	(level 1, appended last in the `iota` list) and `browserStateTags` (level 2).
436	
437	*The form's buttons.* `formButtons()` (`browser_form.go`) is the single source
438	of the buttons: the keyboard, the rendering (`renderFormButtons`, one line) and
439	the header (`FormEnter`) all read it. Without a `Searcher` there is one button,
440	`Browse Tags` (action `actionSearch`). With one there are two, `Search`
441	(`actionSearch`) then `Open Tags` (`actionOpenTags`).
442	
443	*Field indices.* Repository is `brFieldRepo` (0); the picker checkboxes are
444	1..n (n = `len(b.rows)`); the buttons follow: `brFieldButton(i)` = `1 + n + i`,
445	and `brFieldLast()` is the last button. `focusedButton()` maps the focus back to
446	a button (false on Repository or a checkbox). `down` stops at `brFieldLast()`.
447	
448	*Validation.* `submit(action)` is common to both actions: an empty name starts
449	nothing; no registry checked sends `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg{"No registry
450	selected"}`, which the `Model` shows as a footer warning (the browser has no
451	footer; this also applies to a name that contains `/`, where the tag flow used
452	to refuse silently). Then `actionOpenTags` always goes to `startTagLookup`
453	(the former code extracted as is, name as typed). `actionSearch` follows the
454	IS-01 rule: a name with no `/` goes to `startImageSearch` when `b.searcher !=
455	nil`, anything else to `startTagLookup`. `enter` on Repository runs
456	`actionSearch`; `enter` on a button runs that button's action; `enter` on a
457	checkbox only advances the focus. The selection applies to both actions.
458	
459	*Header.* `FormEnter()` returns the label and the lit state of the header's
460	single `enter` entry. The label follows the focus: `Search` on Repository and
461	on the Search button (`Browse tags` without a `Searcher`), `Open tags` on the
462	Open Tags button. `enter` is lit on Repository (Rule 130: it submits there) and
463	on a button, and greyed on a checkbox.
464	
465	*Help.* `registryBrowserHelpBody(searchEnabled)` (`view.go`) depends on the
466	mode (Rule 114): without a `Searcher` it names Browse Tags only; with one it
467	describes Search, Open Tags and the shared selection, and the level 1 sentence.
468	
469	**`defaultImageSearcher` is `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})` in
470	production (DEVDESK-301, IS-02; catalog since DEVDESK-306, IS-03), so level 1
471	and Open Tags are active.** `newRegistryBrowser`
472	copies it into `b.searcher`. Tests do not use it: `TestMain`
473	(`ociresources_test.go`) saves it in `productionImageSearcher` and sets
474	`defaultImageSearcher` to `nil` for the whole suite (no test may reach the real
475	Hub), and tests inject a fake with `withImageSearcher`.
476	`TestProductionWiresTheHubSearcher` reads the saved value. `internal/app`
477	injects nothing: its tests avoid level 1 by typing a name with a `/`.
478	
479	`startImageSearch` runs one `searchImagesCmd` per checked registry, with
480	`targetFor(entry)` (same credentials as the tag flow, `credsFor`). Each command
481	wraps the lot's context in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, imageSearchDeadline)`:
482	`imageSearchDeadline` is 15 s **per registry**, the whole walk included, on top
483	of the 15 s client timeout per request (see the limit above). A registry's
484	answer arrives as `ImageSearchResultMsg{Gen, EntryKey, Images, Partial, Err}`
485	and `AddImageResults` takes it (false when stale; `pendingSearches` never goes
486	under 0).
487	
488	**Verdicts per registry (DEVDESK-303, IS-12).** `AddImageResults` calls
489	`imagesearch.Classify` in `Update`, never in the `Cmd` (Rule 110), and stores the
490	result in `RegistryBrowser.outcomes`, keyed by `EntryKey`. The map is reset by
491	`startImageSearch`, so it holds one lot only; a registry with no entry is still
492	pending. Only an `ok` verdict appends rows. `Outcome(entryKey)` reads one
493	verdict (false while pending). `Model.RegistryBrowserOutcomes()` returns a copy
494	of the map, or nil when the browser is closed; it is for the tests and for IS-13.
495	
496	**Level 1 header summary (DEVDESK-305, IS-13).** `searchHeaderInfo`
497	(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one
498	header line per class, in this order: `Images` (the row count, always), then
499	`Pending` (a count, live lot) or `Interrupted` (names, the lot was abandoned
500	with the left arrow before they answered), `Failed` (red), `Refused`, `Partial`
501	(orange), `Cached only` (orange, DEVDESK-308, IS-14), `No result` (dim) and `Skipped` (dim, catalog not walked because the
502	query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing
503	to say has no line, so a lot where every registry answered shows only `Images`.
504	`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
505	Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
506	`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with
507	nothing (Skipped excluded). A registry that is both partial and empty appears
508	on both lines, on purpose.
509	
510	`Cached only` lists the registries whose list is limited to cached content: a
511	`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, or a member of such a group (a
512	discovered member, or a declared entry whose `parent` is the slug of one).
513	`config.IsNexusGroup` and `listsCacheOnly` decide, once, into

# Container engine, OCI registries, network diagnostics, sockets and interfaces

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

## The container engine — `internal/engine` and `internal/docker`

**`internal/engine`** names the engine in use — docker or podman — and carries
everything that is not the same between the two: the binary, the credential
helper prefix, the auth file, the host socket, and the `--format` templates. It
is its own package rather than a field of `internal/docker` because
`internal/scan` needs the same answer and does not import `internal/docker` —
`internal/forge`'s arrangement read one level down (§3.67).

`engine.Resolve(preference)` turns `app.container_engine` into a `Shape`:
`auto` takes docker if it is on PATH and podman otherwise; a pinned engine that
is absent is an **error**, never the other one, because the two do not hold the
same containers. Anything else is taken as a path to a binary. The router
resolves once at startup and once per context switch, into `engine.SetCurrent`.

A `Shape` carries **no resolved filesystem path**: `AuthPaths()`, `AuthPath()`
and `HostSocket()` are methods. The shape is built at package initialisation, so
a `$HOME` read there would be frozen before anything else runs — and whether the
socket exists is the whole question, since `podman system service` can start or
stop while the application is up.

**`internal/docker`** drives that engine. Every invocation goes through one
seam — `dockerRunner`, implemented by `cliRunner` (`exec.go`) — which is what
made podman cheap: the binary name lived in exactly one place. The package is
split by resource: `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`, `volumes.go`,
`registry.go`, `system.go`, `launch.go`, plus `exec.go` (the seam), `parse.go`,
`container_ports.go`, `identifier.go` and `names.go`. It is **not** called
`internal/container`: renaming it would touch 40 files for a vocabulary gain.

Two things about the engine are worth knowing before changing this code:

- **The `--format` templates are per engine and identical today.** Podman
  implements `--format`, but equality of the *fields* is guaranteed nowhere, and
  a divergence raises no error — it produces wrong rows. No measurement has been
  taken against a real podman; `TestTheTwoTemplateSetsAreStillUnmeasured` fails
  the day the two sets stop matching, so a divergence is recorded deliberately.
- **`system df -v` is scraped, not templated**, and is therefore disabled under
  podman (`Shape.ParsesSystemDFVerbose`). It is a fixed-width table read at
  offsets taken from its header line, and there is no `--format` that exposes
  per-image unique size.

- **Three typed, read-only reads for the Path tab** (`container_network.go`,
  DEVDESK-330), each with a `context.Context` that kills the invocation:
  `InspectContainerNetworking(ctx, id)`, `ListContainersContext(ctx, all)`
  (`ListContainers(all)` is unchanged and does not use it) and
  `EngineOperatingSystem(ctx)`. They run `container inspect`, `ps` and `info`
  and nothing else. `InspectContainerNetworking` runs
  `container inspect --format <containerNetworkingFormat> <id>`: the format
  selects `Name`, `HostConfig.NetworkMode`, `State.Running` and, per network,
  `IPAddress`, `Gateway` and `GwPriority`, so `Config.Env`, labels and mounts are
  never read into memory. It reads stdout only, and its error carries the
  command label, never the output. The ID must pass `IsContainerID` and is one
  argv element, never a name. The inspect and `info` reads refuse a non-Docker
  engine with `ErrDockerOnly` before any invocation; output over 256 KiB
  (`maxInspectBytes`) is refused. `InspectContainer`, which returns the whole
  `docker inspect` JSON (secrets included) with stdout and stderr merged and no
  context, was not reused for that reason. The `info` format
  (`{{.OperatingSystem}}`) is a docker-only literal and is not in
  `engine.Templates`.
- `internal/docker/netdiag.go` — **gone**. §3.33 took the five probes that did not need a container, §3.43 the ports table, §3.44 the topology (and with it `docker/topology.go` and the last `--privileged`), §3.47 the route trace and the file itself (the trace came back in the process as `internal/nettrace`, DEVDESK-327). §3.61 removed the OCI connectivity test, and with it the last container this application runs for a diagnostic: `networks.go` now holds only `ListNetworks`, `CreateNetwork`, `RemoveNetwork`, `PruneNetworks` and `InspectNetwork`.

## OCI registries — `internal/oci`

`internal/oci/oci.go` — an OCI **registry** HTTP client: list tags,
download and extract a tar.gz (a repository template is one — `templates.md`). It speaks the distribution spec over `net/http`
and never shells out, so it is engine-agnostic and podman changed nothing in it.

**Typed status errors and context variants (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** A registry
or token endpoint answering with a non-success status returns
`*oci.StatusError{Code, Source, Challenge}`; read it with `errors.As`. `Source`
is `SourceRegistry` (the v2 API) or `SourceToken` (the Bearer token endpoint).
`Challenge` is the `Www-Authenticate` header of a 401 whose challenge is not
Bearer. `Error()` keeps the three historical messages to the character
(`registry returned 404`, `token endpoint returned 403`,
`unexpected auth challenge: ...`), so nothing on screen or in a log changed.
Failures that are not a status (unreadable body, missing realm, no token
field) stay plain errors and do not match `errors.As`.

The unexported `unexpectedChallenge` field is a deviation from the plan, which
had only `Code`, `Source` and `Challenge`: with those three, a 401 with a
non-Bearer challenge and a 401 returned by the registry after a token exchange
both read `Source == SourceRegistry`, `Code == 401`, and `Error()` could not
give each its own message. The flag tells them apart without widening the
exported surface.

`ListRegistryTagsContext` and the `...Context` variants of `registryGET`,
`registryDo`, `doRequest` and `exchangeBearerToken` take a `context.Context`
(the token endpoint request included) and check `ctx.Err()` at the head of
every page. The old names delegate with `context.Background()`, signatures
unchanged. A deadline or a cancel reaches the caller as an error that
satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` or `context.Canceled`,
and never as a `StatusError`. **Limit:** `registryHTTPClient` keeps its own
`Timeout: 15s` per request, and the client wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`
for that timeout too. A caller cannot tell the client timeout from the
context's deadline, so `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts both in
the `failed` verdict.

**Credentials stay on their origin (DEVDESK-410).** Three guards keep the Basic
credentials and the Bearer token from leaving the registry they were meant for:

- **The tag list never follows a `Link: rel="next"` to another origin.**
  `ListRegistryTagsContext` checks each `next` with `sameOrigin` (the catalog
  walker's guard) before the next request. A foreign `next` is an error that
  wraps `ErrTagsNextOffOrigin` (test it with `errors.Is`) and names the
  destination host only. No partial list is returned: a short list could pass
  for the whole one, and `imageupdate` and the security remediation would read
  a false "up to date". The catalog walker behaves otherwise: it returns
  `truncated=true` with the names already read, and no error.
- **`registryHTTPClient` has a `CheckRedirect`, `refuseOffOriginRedirect`.** A
  redirect is refused when its scheme, host or port differ from the first
  request of the chain (`via[0]`, not only the previous hop), so a chain that
  leaves the origin and comes back is refused too. The error reads
  `refusing redirect to another origin (<host>)` and wraps
  `errOffOriginRedirect` (`errors.Is`). It holds neither the target URL, nor
  its path or query: `redirectRefusal` strips the `*url.Error` that carries
  them, so a signed URL reaches neither the footer nor the logs. The limit of 10 redirects (`maxRedirects`, the `net/http` default) is
  kept. It applies to everything that uses the client: tags, catalog and the
  token endpoint.
- **The token endpoint's answer is capped at 1 MiB** (`maxTokenResponse`). A
  larger body is an error (`token response over 1048576 bytes`), not a silent
  cut.

**Behavior change.** Some redirects that were followed are now refused: `http`
to `https` on the same host, `host` to `host:443`, and a host written with a
different case. The comparison is on the exact scheme and `host:port`, and the
guard refuses when in doubt.

**Catalog walk (DEVDESK-306, IS-03).** `ListCatalogContext(ctx, apiURL,
username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` returns `(names, truncated, err)`. It
asks `<apiURL>/v2/_catalog?n=<pageSize>` and follows `Link: rel="next"` for at
most `maxPages` pages (non-positive limits are an error). `truncated` is true
when names were left: the page cap was reached with a `next` link, more than
`maxPages*pageSize` names came back (the list is cut to that), or the `next`
link points to another origin. Each page body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger
page is an error, not a silent cut. A non-200 answer is a `*StatusError`.
Authentication is the tags' flow: Basic, then Bearer on a challenge, the token
kept across pages.

- **`next` is followed only to the same origin.** `sameOrigin` compares scheme
  and host strictly (`host` and `host:443` differ), so a registry cannot make
  the walk send the Basic credentials or the token elsewhere. A foreign or
  differently written `next` ends the walk as `truncated`, with no error.
- **HTTP 3xx redirects are hardened too** (DEVDESK-410): the walk goes through
  `registryHTTPClient`, whose `CheckRedirect` refuses a redirect to another
  origin (see "Credentials stay on their origin" above).

## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)

Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:

- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
  an anonymous entry, D12).
- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
  `library/` applied once (D39).
- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
  with no request at all. Production uses
  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` and
  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
  registry. Steps, in order:
  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
     is returned as is, with no row.
  3. Guard R1 (before the filter): when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
     `partial` set, not an error.
  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
     others are dropped.
  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.

  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search
  (DEVDESK-311, IS-07, `walks.go`): `WithSharedWalks(ctx)` puts a memo on the
  batch context and `CatalogSearcher` goes through `walkCatalog`, so a search
  queries `/v2/_catalog` once per API URL and identity. Without the memo
  (any other caller) every call walks on its own.
  - Key: the exact API URL (trailing slash ignored) and the identity, an
    HMAC-SHA256 of username and password under a random per-batch key: no
    secret is held in clear and the key prints no userinfo. Two identities
    never share a walk, because Harbor, Artifactory and GitLab filter the
    catalog per account. A `credentials` entry with no effective secret shares
    the walk of an anonymous entry. A member on another port or subdomain has
    another API URL and is not grouped.
  - Leader and followers: the first call for a key walks, the others wait (or
    return on their own context). It is a memo, not a singleflight: the key is
    kept after the walk, so a member arriving later reuses the result, and it
    dies with the batch (no cache between two searches).
  - A shared failure (a 503, say) is the same error for every member, so the
    same verdict (`failed` or `refused`), one message per entry. A result
    caused by the leader's own context ending is not memoized: followers
    already waiting on that flight receive the leader's context error (verdict
    `failed`), and only members arriving afterwards walk again. A
    panic in the leader gives followers a sentinel error (`errWalkAborted`),
    never an empty catalog.
  - `repo_prefix` filtering, `partial`, `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` and
    `Cached only` stay computed per member.
  - Unverified assumption: members of one host answer on the same
    `/v2/_catalog` (IS-16).
  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
  match wins:
  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
     given in both cases;
  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
     token endpoint is a failure); any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is
     `failed`;
  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
     oversized body, invalid request.

  `ErrQueryTooShort` and `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` are returned by
  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).

## Image updates — `internal/imageupdate` (§3.88)

Three tables carry an **Update** column (`internal/ui/updatecol`): oci's Images
tab, the containers list, and the Remediation tab of a scan result. It shows an
arrow when the image's registry holds something newer, and says what:

| Kind | When | Cell |
|---|---|---|
| `NewPatch` | the tag has ≥ 3 version components and a tag differing only by the last, same variant, is higher (`20.11.1-alpine` → `20.11.4-alpine`) | the arrow and the tag |
| `NewBuild` | the digest the tag points to now is none of the local image's digests | the arrow alone (`IconArrowDown`) |

A newer patch wins over a new build. Every other state says why there is no
arrow, in grey — a blank used to stand for all of them, which in the
Remediation tab (bases rarely pinned, often not held locally) meant a column
that was silent without saying why:

| Kind | Cell | When |
|---|---|---|
| `UpToDate` | the check mark | the local digest is the tag's |
| `Pending` | `IconHourglass` | no answer yet |
| `Failed` | `IconHelpCircle` | the registry did not answer (logged) |
| `LocalBuild` | `IconHammer` | images, containers: no registry digest |
| `NotLocal` | `IconCloud` | Remediation: unpinned, and not held by the engine |
| `Pinned` | `IconPin` | a digest with no tag: nothing can move |
| `None` | blank | the question does not apply (untagged image, unresolved `FROM`) |

Every state but a newer patch is one glyph (`updatecol.Cell`): the words cost
eleven cells in the widest table there is, and the reason is still spelled out
by `G`'s greyed shortcut in the footer and by `?`. `Status.Label` keeps the
word, which is what the filter matches. `Evaluate` takes what "no local digest"
means to its caller (`LocalBuild` or `NotLocal`). The column's filter only matches an update's label, or `/ca`
would find every `local build`. A tag with fewer components (`3.20`,
`20`) has no patches of its own — it floats over them, so a new patch moves the
tag and the digest says it. That is also the only answer a floating tag
(§3.79) ever gets.

**The registry's side is cached, the comparison is not.** `imageupdate.Check`
keeps, per reference, the tag's digest and the newer patch tag in
`~/.devdesk/cache/image-updates.json` — 6 hours for an answer, 30 minutes for a
failure (unknown repository, no credentials) so it is not asked on every
refresh. `Evaluate` compares with the local digests each time a row is built,
so a pull clears the arrow without asking the registry again.

**Two requests at most per reference.** The digest is a `HEAD` on the manifest
(`oci.ManifestDigest`) accepting an OCI index and a Docker manifest list — a
multi-platform tag's digest is the index's, the one `docker pull` records in
`RepoDigests`. Docker Hub does not count a `HEAD` against its pull rate limit.
The tag list (`oci.ListRegistryTags`) is only read for a tag with a patch
component. At most four references are asked at once; credentials are the
engine's (`docker.GetStoredCreds`), as for the Remediation tab.

**What each view compares with:**

- *Images* — the image's own `RepoDigests`, now read by the same `image
  inspect` that reads its size (`templates().ImageInspect`). Only a tagged image
  **with** a digest is asked about: one built or loaded here has none, and its
  name would send the question to a registry that never heard of it.
- *Containers* — the digests of the image the container was **created from**
  (`docker.ContainerImageDigests`: `container inspect` for the image ID, then
  `image inspect`). After a pull the container still runs the old image, so the
  arrow stays until it is recreated — which is what it is there to say. The
  digests are read again only when the set of containers changes, not on every
  two-second refresh.
- *Remediation* — the digest the Dockerfile pins, or else the image the engine
  holds under that name (`docker.ImageRepoDigests`). A base the engine does not
  hold only gets the patch side.

`imageupdate.Tracker` is what each view keeps between checks: the facts it has
and the references a check is out for, so a reload asks only what is new or
stale. Every view reaches the network through a package variable its tests
replace.

**Updating — `G` on the Images tab.** It pulls what the column points at (the
newer patch tag, or the same tag again for a new build) and removes the image
it replaces, by ID and never forced. It refuses while any container, running
or stopped, was created from that image (`docker.ContainersUsingImage`, `ps -a
--filter ancestor=`): removing it would break the container, and keeping it
would leave the update half done. The check is made twice — from the engine's
container count to grey `G` (Rule 130; docker only, podman reports none), and
against the engine just before the pull, since a container can appear in
between. A pull that brings the image already held removes nothing
(`docker.SameImageID`). It runs as a pull job, so the row spins and `K` stops
it; every refusal and failure is a footer line naming why (the containers in
use, a failed pull, an old image that could not be removed).

**On a narrow terminal**, the containers table drops the two gauges before
Update (they are `DropFirst`, §3.71), then the I/O counters, then Update. Both
gauges now need 180 columns instead of 160.

**Not done**: a digest for a tag the engine holds under another name, and the
`podman` side of `RepoDigests` has not been measured against a real `podman
system service` — the field exists there under the same name.

**From a container to its image — `J`** (§3.89). The containers view sends
`ociresources.FocusImageRequestMsg` with the image reference exactly as the
engine printed it; the router switches to the OCI view and hands it the
request, which waits for the first listing if the view was just built
(`deferUntilListed`, the same queue agents use). Matching is the OCI view's
(`imageMatches`, `focus.go`): an implicit `latest`, docker's `nginx` against
podman's `docker.io/library/nginx`, a registry port that is not a tag, a
`repo@sha256:` digest against `RepoDigests`, and a bare ID — what `ps` shows
once the tag has moved to a newer image. A search hiding the target is
dropped; an image that is no longer listed is a footer `Warn`. There is no
`esc` back: `:ct` returns, as from any other view.

## The OCI tables and the activity column — `internal/ui/oci_resources` (DEVDESK-146, A-09a; DEVDESK-153, A-09b)

The four tables of `:oci` (Images, Networks, Volumes, Registries) and the
registry browser's tag table are on the activity column (Rule 125; the router
side is in `app-shell.md`).

**Periodic refresh and terminal focus (DEVDESK-210).** `refreshInterval` is 10 s
(a var, so a test can shorten it). `RefreshTickMsg` used to refresh once and
never again; it now re-arms `tickCmd()` on every tick. While `Model.blurred` is
set (from `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`) the tick only re-arms and skips
`refreshReads()` (images, scan cache, networks, volumes; it never scans, Rule
126). On the focus edge (`Resume`) it runs `refreshReads()` once, with no new tick.

**Registry browser (DEVDESK-218, A-09a2).** The tag table
(`registry_browser.go`, built by `newTagTable`, which `ActivityTables` also uses
so the guard sees the real table open or not, as `oci/registry-browser`) takes
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0, an 8th column; Registry, Tag and
Updated are 1 to 3 (`tagColumnTag` = 2, `tagColumnUpdated` = 3). `tagRow` holds
`Activity components.RowActivity` and `ScanRunning`, stamped by
`rebuildTagTable` from `components.DescribeRow` (scan and pull, `ociKinds`,
target `jobs.TargetKey(imageName)`) over the snapshot the router pushes through
`SetJobs(runs, failures, context)`; the cell at rest is empty. While a scan
really runs (not queued) the C/H/M/L cells hold `…` in `DimStyle`; a queued scan
or a pull keeps the counts. The blink phase arrives with `SetBlinkPhase` and
`WantsBlink` is true for a visible running tag row. Rule 116: Updated drops
under 102 columns, L under 84, M under 78, H under 72, C under 66; at 60 only
the dot, Registry and Tag remain. The browser has no spinner of its own
(DEVDESK-374): a search shows the shared activity dot in the footer
(`Searching registries...`), and `WantsBlink` is true while it runs. After the search the
footer describes the selected tag (`Status{Detail}`). `tagScanSpinnerIdx` and
the local frame are deleted. `DescribeRow` filters by context: a scan of another
context no longer shows on a tag (D108).

**Cancelling a lot and ignoring late answers (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** The
browser launches requests in lots (one per validation that starts something).
`browserGen` is a package-wide `atomic.Uint64`, incremented only from `Update`
(`nextBrowserGen`). `beginRequests()` cancels the previous lot (one
`CancelFunc`, `cancelRequests`, per lot, not per registry), takes a new
generation and resets `pendingSearches`; the `context` is born in `Update`
(Rule 110). `MultiRegistryTagsLoadedMsg`, `MultiRegistryTagsMetaMsg` and
`ImageSearchResultMsg` carry the `Gen` they were started with, and their
handlers return before logging anything when it differs from the open
browser's. The counter is global rather than per browser so that a browser
closed and reopened, or a new `Model` after a context switch, cannot accept the
answer of an older instance. `closeMultiRegistryBrowser` calls
`cancelInFlight()`, which also covers closing through `G` (a pull). A validation
that starts nothing (empty name, no registry checked) cancels nothing and
leaves `gen` alone. The tag lookups go through the `listRegistryTags` variable
(`oci.ListRegistryTagsContext`), the seam tests swap to capture the context;
there is no deadline on a tag lookup, only `maxTagPages` and the per-request
client timeout. `Model.RegistryBrowserGen()` exposes the generation to tests
only.

**Level 1: image search (DEVDESK-299, IS-01; Open Tags DEVDESK-300, IS-11).**
The browser has three states: `browserStateInput` (form), `browserStateImages`
(level 1, appended last in the `iota` list) and `browserStateTags` (level 2).

*The form's buttons.* `formButtons()` (`browser_form.go`) is the single source
of the buttons: the keyboard, the rendering (`renderFormButtons`, one line) and
the header (`FormEnter`) all read it. Without a `Searcher` there is one button,
`Browse Tags` (action `actionSearch`). With one there are two, `Search`
(`actionSearch`) then `Open Tags` (`actionOpenTags`).

*Field indices.* Repository is `brFieldRepo` (0); the picker checkboxes are
1..n (n = `len(b.rows)`); the buttons follow: `brFieldButton(i)` = `1 + n + i`,
and `brFieldLast()` is the last button. `focusedButton()` maps the focus back to
a button (false on Repository or a checkbox). `down` stops at `brFieldLast()`.

*Validation.* `submit(action)` is common to both actions: an empty name starts
nothing; no registry checked sends `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg{"No registry
selected"}`, which the `Model` shows as a footer warning (the browser has no
footer; this also applies to a name that contains `/`, where the tag flow used
to refuse silently). Then `actionOpenTags` always goes to `startTagLookup`
(the former code extracted as is, name as typed). `actionSearch` follows the
IS-01 rule: a name with no `/` goes to `startImageSearch` when `b.searcher !=
nil`, anything else to `startTagLookup`. `enter` on Repository runs
`actionSearch`; `enter` on a button runs that button's action; `enter` on a
checkbox only advances the focus. The selection applies to both actions.

*Header.* `FormEnter()` returns the label and the lit state of the header's
single `enter` entry. The label follows the focus: `Search` on Repository and
on the Search button (`Browse tags` without a `Searcher`), `Open tags` on the
Open Tags button. `enter` is lit on Repository (Rule 130: it submits there) and
on a button, and greyed on a checkbox.

*Help.* `registryBrowserHelpBody(searchEnabled)` (`view.go`) depends on the

## Verified pulls — `internal/imagepull` (§3.82)

**Every pull goes through `imagepull.Pull`** — the registry browser's `G`, an
update's `G`, an agent's `image_pull_start`. `TestNoPullBypassesTheSignatureCheck`
(`internal/ui/oci_resources`) walks `internal/` and fails on any other file
naming `docker.PullImageContext`: a second path would be a pull nobody
verified. The engine's pull survives in the OCI view only as the seam
`pullImageContext`, handed to `imagepull.Deps` by `pullDeps` and called nowhere.

The sequence, in `pull.go`:

1. `scan.image_verification: off` pulls the tag, as before §3.82.
2. `~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` is read on every pull. A file that does not load
   **refuses** the pull, naming the error: an unreadable policy is not an empty
   one, and falling back to the built-in rules would drop the user's in silence.
3. The tag is resolved to a digest (`oci.ManifestDigest`, the index digest
   cosign signs). A registry that will not give it is a Failed verdict decided
   by the rule that would have applied — a user rule refuses, anything else
   pulls the tag and warns.
4. `trust.Evaluate` on that digest, with the local image of the same repository
   (`RepoDigests`) for continuity. `Block` is an `imagepull.BlockedError`,
   whose message is the reason, naming the rule.
5. `pull repo@digest`, then `docker.TagImage` back to the name asked for.
   Pulling the tag instead would let it move between the check and the pull —
   the attack. Measured on Docker and Podman; under Docker's containerd store
   `repo@sha256:…` also shows in `RepoTags`, `docker images` lists one row.

What the views do with it: a refusal is a footer **Error** naming the rule, and
the `:jobs` detail an agent reads is the same sentence; a Warn goes ahead and
says why after the pull. The Images tab header shows `Signatures: off`, or
`trust.yaml invalid` — read once when the view starts (`checkTrustPolicyCmd`).

**The `Sig` column** of the Images tab (`signatures.go`, the shared
`internal/ui/sigcol`) is each local image's verdict on the content on disk:
`imagepull.LocalDigest` picks the `RepoDigests` entry of the image's own
repository, and `imagepull.Check` asks about that digest against the rules
alone — continuity would compare the image with itself. An image with no such
digest was built or loaded here (a hammer, as in Update). Checked in the
background on `ImagesListMsg`, four at a time; `sigAsked` keeps the digest each
image was asked about, so an unchanged list asks nothing, a pull that changes
the digest asks again, a verdict about a former digest is dropped, and a Failed
one is retried after 30 minutes. An image no rule covers is decided without
cosign, and one DevDesk pulled comes from the verdict cache. Nothing acts on
the column.

**`run` never pulls**: `buildLaunchArgs` and `VerifyEntrypoint` pass
`--pull=never` (a missing image exits 125, both engines). An image reaches the
machine through a verified pull or not at all. DevDesk's own tool images —
Trivy, cosign, the netdiag image — are pulled by their `run` and are **not**
verified: a declared exception.
